title: About MITIME
intro:
MITIME, *Entanglements of Migration and Time in Post-industrial Urban Europe*, is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network coordinated by the University of Oulu. It brings together seven universities of the UNIC alliance of post-industrial cities and seven non-academic partners to train a new generation of migration scholars.

The network treats time as a resource that is unequally distributed. Waiting for papers, working on temporary contracts or living with an uncertain future all shape how people can make a life in the city. MITIME also follows the call to *de-migranticise* research: to study how institutions, discourses and practices produce “the migrant”, rather than treating migrants as a problem to be explained.

agendas.title: Time and the everyday
agendas.text: How temporal insecurity shapes social ties, work, homemaking, narratives and everyday bordering.

agendas.title: Time and institutions
agendas.text: How states, employers, cities and other institutions govern and sort people through time.

agendas.title: Time and future-making
agendas.text: How migrants, communities and cities imagine and build their futures.

themes.name: Connectivities
themes.text: How temporal in/security shapes social, material and digital connections.

themes.name: Labour
themes.text: Precarious work, temporal precarity and the institutional temporal order of labour.

themes.name: Placemaking
themes.text: Homemaking, border temporalities and diasporic identifications.

themes.name: Narrative
themes.text: Memory, displacement and the collective narratives cities tell about themselves.

themes.name: Governance
themes.text: How policies, services and citizenship regimes govern migration through time.
